answer: A fishing harbor gives each agent one boat that leaves only on the outgoing tide and carries a numbered lantern on its mast. The crew fishes through the night, brings the catch to the dock at dawn, and a clerk weighs it against the boat log and checks the lantern number when the morning market reaches its zenith, with every boat back in port. A second boat under the same name loses both berths for a season. Faking a thousand names means buying a thousand boats and landing a thousand weighed catches night after night, while a clerk checks each lantern.
